quotes.text: This controls the allowed types instead of selecting a single default payment method.
For `send_invoice`, customers can select from the eligible payment method types when they pay on the Hosted Invoice Page.
For `charge_automatically`, Stripe attempts payment without first showing the customer a payment method selector.
Stripe also attempts to include the type of the applicable default payment method and filters the result based on eligibility for the invoice.
If you explicitly configure an ineligible type, Stripe might return an error when creating or updating the subscription or finalizing an invoice.

old_evidence.text: If set, a subscription’s `payment_settings.payment_method_types` takes priority over default invoice settings, but only for that specific subscription.
The new payment method must be a card.
If unused, a link expires after 30 days.

findings: The November capture clarifies the object as subscription payment_settings.payment_method_types: it limits allowed method types, not a specific payment method or the single default (new 5-9). This preserves the old per-subscription override at old 16-36 but warrants narrowing current source 13/27's references to individual PMs to types where they describe the setting.

The new guide explicitly distinguishes collection_method: send_invoice permits a customer to select eligible types on the Hosted Invoice Page, whereas charge_automatically first attempts payment without a selector and limits the invoice PaymentIntent's usable types; later invoice or recovery flows expose only eligible types (new 11-14). It adds account activation and recurring/product support prerequisites (new 16-21), and eligibility by currency, amount, country, collection method and product support (new 61-65). Neither the API sample at new 44-55 nor Dashboard steps at 33-40 proves a payment succeeded.

Default behavior is more qualified than current source's simple priority list: Stripe derives generated-invoice types from Invoice default settings, attempts to include the applicable default method's type, then filters for invoice eligibility; explicit subscription types take precedence for that subscription and pass to its SetupIntent and invoices (new 25-27). The new warning says that if a subscription uses a default method, its type must be included or that default cannot pay its invoices (new 57-59). Source 31-33 should not imply an unconditional ordered payment-attempt chain; the old guide separately says default_payment_method or legacy default_source can prioritize which method is attempted (old 34-38).

The new Dashboard path is specifically creation with emailed manual invoices (new 31-40); the new API example creates a subscription using an existing customer and recurring price, with a restricted key requiring subscription_write permission (new 42-55). The May sample instead updates an existing subscription (old 18-28). These are documented sample/UI contexts, not evidence that the update API was removed or that Dashboard only supports manual invoice configuration.

The May guide describes Dashboard payment-update links for automatically billed subscriptions, available only at active/past_due/trialing, card-only, one use, 30 days if unused, scoped to that subscription rather than the customer's default (old 42-61). It also documents save_default_payment_method behavior (old 40). These sections are absent from the November capture; absence alone is not deprecation or a current guarantee. Retain those claims as dated May evidence in source 13/35-48 and concept stripe-subscriptions-invoices 109-111 with a reciprocal qualification rather than silently removing them.

The May error discussion says restrictions or inactive methods can prevent creation, and errors can arise at payment/finalization (old 63-70). The November text uses modal 'might' for an explicitly configured ineligible type returning an error at creation, update or invoice finalization (new 61-65). Source 52-54's categorical arrow from restriction to failed creation should be narrowed to a possible failure and reflect update/finalization stages. No account-specific eligibility, successful collection or invoice finality is established by either capture.
substantive_changes: November text sharpens allowed payment method types versus a selected default, and adds collection_method-specific customer/automatic flow behavior and invoice eligibility filtering (new 9-14, 25-27, 57-65).

November guide adds a Dashboard create-with-email-invoice path and API subscription-create example, unlike the May subscription-update example; neither example establishes that the other operation was removed (new 31-55; old 18-28).
Current source needs correction to qualify its priority and error statements (source 27, 31-33, 52-54) and date its May-only update-link/save-default claims (source 13, 35-48).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 2026 documentation of the subscriptions.update example with card/customer_balance types, legacy default_source prioritization and Dashboard/Subscription save-default behavior as dated (old 18-40).
Preserve May 2026 Dashboard payment-update-link restrictions only as dated historical guide content, not as a November-confirmed availability guarantee or proof of deprecation (old 42-61).

Preserve the old distinction between method-type inclusion and an individual default method: omitting the default's type can make that method unusable and payment might fail (old 30); November restates the default-type warning with invoice eligibility context (new 25, 57-59).
conflicts: Source 31-33 presents payment-method types, Invoice default settings and legacy default_source as a three-step payment priority order. Old 34-38 distinguishes allowed-type precedence from default-method attempt priority; new 25-27 adds eligibility filtering. These cannot safely be collapsed into one unconditional chain.

Source 52-54 says a currency/amount restriction leads to subscription creation failure; new 65 says an ineligible explicit type might error at creation, update or invoice finalization, while old 65-70 also includes payment-time failure. Narrow the categorical claim.

Source 13/35-48 and invoice concept 109-111 state payment-update-link and save-default details without a May-only provenance warning, while the November page omits those topics. Omission does not prove removal or current support.
unresolved_questions: The assigned November capture does not readdress payment-update-link availability, card-only and 30-day restrictions, default-saving behavior, or legacy default_source; those remain dated May claims pending separate current authority.
Eligibility and exact error timing depend on the account, method, currency, country, amount and collection method; no live account or invoice outcome was observed.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/payment-methods-setting, the November guide defines subscription payment_settings.payment_method_types as allowed types rather than one default method (new 5-9). The collection method determines customer selection versus automatic PaymentIntent attempts, and eligibility depends on activation, currency, amount, country and support (new 11-21, 61-65). Explicit types override Invoice default settings for that subscription; Stripe otherwise attempts to include the applicable default type but filters for invoice eligibility (new 25-27, 57-59). The May guide in [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]] also covered subscriptions.update, default_source, save-default settings and Dashboard update links (old 18-61). The current source's priority and error shorthand needs qualification; no capture proves payment success or account-specific eligibility.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/payment-methods-setting, the substantive additions are method-type identity, collection_method flow differences, eligibility filtering and modal error timing (new 9-14, 25-27, 61-65). The Dashboard manual-invoice creation steps and API create sample replace the May update example in presentation, not demonstrably in API capability (new 31-55; old 18-28). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]] should correct its simplistic priority ladder at 31-33 and categorical creation-failure arrow at 52-54. Its save-default and payment-update-link claims at 35-48, echoed in the invoice concept, belong to the May capture (old 40-61); the new page's silence is not deprecation or current confirmation. The Dashboard steps are a specific UI path, the API sample requires a customer, recurring price and appropriate restricted-key permission, and neither shows successful billing or final invoice payment.
